name: Kavala
title: Kavala Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging | Tankers, Bulk & Cargo
description: Ship thickness measurement in Kavala, northern Aegean: UTM for tankers, bulk carriers and cargo ships, hold, deck and ballast tank gauging.
h1: Kavala: Ultrasonic Hull Gauging in the Northern Aegean
intro: Kavala is a northern Aegean port in eastern Macedonia, used by bulk carriers, tankers, general cargo ships and ferries to the island of Thasos. Cargoes here are industrial and seasonal, and many ships are older working tonnage. Readings are fitted to cargo calls and to time at anchor in the bay. A team travels from India to the ship, and the scope is set in advance.

highlights.p: Fertiliser, bulk raw materials and refined products pass through Kavala, which suits readings taken hold by hold as cargo is cleared, plus deck and coaming gauging whenever covers are open.
Oil and gas activity in the northern Aegean brings tankers and service vessels to the area. Deck, piping and ballast tank gauging fits tanker calls within terminal rules.
There is no large repair yard in the area, so gauging here prepares ships for docking elsewhere. Measured readings give the owner a steel estimate before the ship sails for a yard.

port.h: Kavala: a northern Aegean port with an industrial hinterland
p: Kavala sits on the coast of eastern Macedonia, facing the island of Thasos across a narrow strait. The main port is built around a sheltered harbour at the foot of the old town, with commercial quays and a ferry terminal, and the Kavala Port Authority handles the commercial side. Beyond the central harbour there is an industrial area to the east, around Nea Karvali, where tankers and other ships work at private jetties, and there are ferry connections to Thasos from Kavala and from Keramoti further east along the coast.

The ships that visit are mixed. Bulk carriers load and discharge raw materials and agricultural products, general cargo ships serve regional industry, product tankers supply fuel and carry refined products, and ro-pax ferries run to Thasos in the season. The northern Aegean also has offshore oil and gas activity, which brings tankers, service craft and supply vessels to the area. A good share of the ships involved are older tonnage on regional trades, which means local wear on holds, hatch covers and coamings from the cargo handled, and wastage on weather decks and ballast tanks from long service.

The northern Aegean has its own weather. Cold northerly winds in winter can be strong, and summer meltemi episodes affect the strait. Ships at anchor in the bay are normally well sheltered, but launch transfers depend on conditions, and tank entry preparations must be finished before the window starts. Because the region lacks a major repair centre, ships needing steel work usually leave for yards in Thessaloniki's area, central Greece or the Athens zones, and gauging at Kavala is valuable as an early picture of hull condition.

facilities.h: Where gauging can be done around Kavala
p: In the commercial harbour, gauging is done alongside at the cargo quays and the ferry terminal, subject to the port authority's ISPS rules and arranged through the agent. A bulk carrier discharging gives access to emptied holds, hatch covers and coamings in sequence, while a general cargo ship offers tank top, side shell and frames once holds are clear. A ferry alongside for the day allows deck, ramp and accessible plating readings, with tank work reserved for lay-up.

Industrial jetties and the anchorage extend the options. Tankers at the energy and fuel terminals are limited to deck, deck piping and ballast spaces within permit rules, and ships at anchor in the bay can be boarded by launch for pre-docking or condition gauging. There is no large drydock in the area, so heavy steel renewal is done elsewhere. For anyone arranging ship inspection in northern Greece, Kavala works best as a staging post where readings are collected before the ship moves to its yard.
list: Commercial cargo quays — hold, hatch cover, coaming and deck gauging on bulk and general cargo ships during discharge
Ferry terminal — deck, ramp and ballast tank readings on Thasos ferries, best during lay-up
Industrial jetties near Nea Karvali — deck, piping and ballast tank gauging on tankers and cargo ships within terminal rules
Kavala Bay anchorage — pre-docking and condition gauging on ships waiting for berths or orders, by launch
Lay-up positions — extended programmes on ships idle between seasons or charters

context.h: Port state control and regional trade
p: Port state control at Kavala is carried out by the Hellenic Coast Guard under the Paris MoU. The Mediterranean emission control area for sulphur, in force since 1 May 2025, includes the Aegean, so ships here burn 0.10% sulphur fuel or run an exhaust gas cleaning system. EU ETS has applied to shipping since 2024 and FuelEU Maritime since 2025, and both cover voyages calling at Kavala. Ships on regional runs may also need an Inventory of Hazardous Materials aboard when calling at EU ports.

Trade patterns in this part of Greece shape the work. Raw materials and industrial products bring bulk carriers and general cargo ships whose owners often have no superintendent attending, so the report needs to be clear and usable without a visit: readings tied to frame numbers, photographs of the worst areas and a short summary of what needs attention. The northern Aegean energy sector adds tanker and service traffic with its own vetting expectations, and owners of those ships may ask for gauging before a charter inspection.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Kavala
jobs.p: Most Kavala jobs are shaped by the cargo call. The superintendent tells us which holds or tanks will be accessible and when, we plan readings to follow the discharge or loading sequence, and we send results area by area so the rest can be scheduled for the next call or the yard.
list: Hold and hatch cover gauging on a bulk carrier discharging at the cargo quay, taking readings hold by hold as each is cleared.
Deck plating and deck piping readings on a product tanker at an industrial jetty, ahead of a vetting inspection.
Pre-docking gauging of ballast tanks on an older general cargo ship at anchor in the bay, giving the manager a steel estimate for a yard elsewhere in Greece.
Pre-purchase condition gauging on a coastal tanker alongside, with the buyer's surveyor attending.
Deck, ramp and ballast tank readings on a Thasos ferry during winter lay-up, supporting the refit specification.

logistics: Teams fly into Kavala's Alexander the Great Airport near Chrysoupoli, usually connecting via Athens or another European hub, or into Thessaloniki and continue by road. Port passes, any launch boarding and jetty permits are arranged by the ship's agent from the crew list and equipment details we send ahead. Technicians need a Schengen visa issued in India, since Greece follows the Schengen rules. Cargo calls here are often fixed at short notice, so flagging likely Kavala visits early lets us keep a visa ready when the berth date firms up.

faqs.q: Can holds be gauged while a bulk carrier is discharging at Kavala?
faqs.a: Yes, hold by hold. Once a hold is emptied and swept, we can measure tank top, hopper and side plating and frames with access arranged by the ship. Any hold still carrying cargo waits for a later call or for the yard. We agree the sequence with the master and the agent so gauging follows the cargo work.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Kavala for steel renewal?
faqs.a: No large drydock is available. Ships needing hull steel work usually go to yards near Thessaloniki, in central Greece or around Athens. Gauging at Kavala is therefore preparation: readings give the owner a steel estimate, help compare yard offers and let plate be ordered before the ship sails.

faqs.q: Can ships at anchor in Kavala Bay be gauged?
faqs.a: Yes. The agent books a launch and we board with portable equipment, though transfers depend on sea state and the master's decision. Tanks must be ventilated, tested and certified before entry. We leave slack in the schedule for northerly weather and tell the superintendent early if the window narrows.

faqs.q: What can be done on a tanker at an industrial jetty?
faqs.a: Normally the deck, its piping and the ballast tanks, under the permit rules of the jetty operator. Work may pause during cargo transfer. The agent and the terminal confirm what is allowed, and we plan readings to fit around discharge rather than hold it up.

faqs.q: Can one trip cover Kavala and Thessaloniki or Alexandroupoli?
faqs.a: Often. All three lie in northern Greece and can be linked by road or a short flight, so one mobilisation can cover several ships if their dates line up. Send us the vessels and windows, and we will plan the order of jobs and visa period together.
